root_motivation: Bootstrap a load-bearing tool autobuilder needs: every iteration's unfakeable scalar must be emitted by a binary that was itself built under autobuilder's verified loop. The current shell-script fallback is a crack in the trust model — until the metric harness is owned by autobuilder, the loop's advance/revert decisions are only as trustworthy as a bash file with no tests.
user_persona: The autobuilder skill (specifically the Stage 3 loop runner) and per-project run-metrics.sh authors. No human invokes this binary directly except for debugging.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a project path, invoke <path>/scripts/run-metrics.sh. Return non-zero (exit 2) if missing or not executable, with stderr identifying the missing script.
Capture project script's stdout AND stderr into <path>/target/autobuilder/run.log.
Parse <path>/target/autobuilder/metrics.json, validate against the autobuilder.metrics.v1 schema embedded as a build-time const. Return exit 3 with a JSON diagnostic on validation failure.

Emit a normalized autobuilder.metrics.v1 document to stdout AND overwrite <path>/target/autobuilder/metrics.json with the same content. Include head_sha (from --head-sha flag), iteration (from --iteration N), scalars, ac_passing_count, ac_total_count, audit.{blocking_count,advisory_count}, clippy_warning_count, captured_at (RFC3339), output_digest (sha256 of canonical JSON excluding output_digest itself).

Exit 0 only if project script exited 0 AND audit.blocking_count == 0 AND ac_results.length == ac_total_count. Otherwise exit 1 — but emit the metrics document either way so the loop can record the failed iteration.
Operate without modifying anything outside <path>/target/autobuilder/. Snapshot-hash the project before and after; only target/autobuilder/* paths may have changed.
Support --iteration N; pass through to metrics.iteration. Default null when absent.
Time-bound the project script with --timeout-seconds N (default 600). On timeout: kill the process, emit metrics with failure_kind="timeout", exit 1.
When project script exits non-zero with no metrics.json produced, emit a synthetic metrics doc with failure_kind in {build_error, metric_emission_failure} so the loop can write a FailureCapsule.
Support --pretty for human-readable stdout; default is single-line canonical JSON. Verifiable by counting newlines in output.

scope: Compute output_digest over the normalized doc
non_goals: Edit scripts/run-metrics.sh or any project file outside target/autobuilder/
Verify git state or invoke git commands (loop runner passes --head-sha)
Retry the project harness (one call, one result)
Remote project paths or URL inputs

additional.allowed_deps: serde, serde_json, anyhow, clap, sha2, std
additional.crate_location: crates/metric-harness/ of the autobuilder workspace (initially scaffolded as a standalone project at /home/jsy/projects/autobuilder-metric-harness/ and vendored in once green)
additional.canonical_json: recursive key-sort + serde_json::to_vec, documented in README
additional.head_sha_source: --head-sha CLI flag; binary does not invoke git

five_whys_trace.q: Why build a metric-harness binary as the first dogfood target rather than picking an external PRD?
five_whys_trace.a: Because every subsequent autobuilder run will use it — making it both maximally dogfooded and load-bearing.

five_whys_trace.q: Why make a load-bearing tool the first one autobuilder builds, rather than something throwaway?
five_whys_trace.a: Because the trust model demands that the binary producing the unfakeable scalar be itself produced by autobuilder's verified loop. Until that's true, there's a shell-script-shaped crack at the foundation of the trust chain.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the trust chain matter so much — can't we just have well-tested shell scripts?
five_whys_trace.a: Because the whole project's premise is 'every Rust artifact is generated under a falsifiable loop with structured receipts.' A shell-script harness in the receipt path means the most load-bearing measurement (the scalar that drives advance/revert) has the weakest validation. The system is only as honest as its weakest link.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Standalone crate vs subcommand of the autobuilder binary?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Standalone crate at crates/metric-harness/. Initially scaffolded to /home/jsy/projects/autobuilder-metric-harness/ for the iterate loop, vendored into the workspace post-green.

ambiguities_resolved.question: How does the harness know head_sha?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: --head-sha CLI flag from caller. No git dependency in the harness; matches the non-goal 'does not verify git state.'

ambiguities_resolved.question: Canonical JSON algorithm for output_digest?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Recursive key-sort + serde_json::to_vec. Fits the tight-deps constraint. Documented in the binary's README.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does the harness own clippy.json parsing?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No — trust the project script's clippy_warning_count. The harness only validates shape, not the gate logic itself.
